Subject: Assistant output IP & APAC residency — quick Q

Hi Priyom,

Quick context: were evaluating Redwood for our customer-facing assistant that will operate in APAC (SG, HK, AU). Two items came up from procurement/security:

1) Ownership and downstream use of prompts/responses: does BrightAssist retain exclusive ownership of prompts we send and the assistant responses? Can Redwood use prompts or responses to improve models, even in aggregated/pseudonymized form?

2) Data residency and cross-border transfer: for Singapore customers we need assurance that customer content does not leave APAC or, if transfers occur, what legal mechanisms are used (SCCs, adequacy, or customer-controlled keys).

Procurement asked for sample DPA language and any evidence we can point to showing implementation (diagrams, subprocessor list, KMS options). We fall under healthcare-adjacent regulation in SG so this is prioritized.

Were hoping for short answers and a next-step plan (contract language + tech path) by early next week.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Klein
Head of Product Operations, BrightAssist

From: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Sara Klein <sara@brightassist.ai>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-31T12:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Assistant output IP & APAC residency — quick Q

Sara, thanks for the clear list — appreciate the timeline. Short answers below, followed by proposed next steps.

1) Ownership: BrightAssist retains rights to your prompts and generated assistant responses. Redwood does not claim ownership of customer content or assistant outputs. We can include explicit IP language in the DPA/SOW to reflect exclusive output ownership.

2) Model improvement: by default our hosted platform collects aggregated telemetry to improve the serving runtime and model performance. However, we offer a contractual opt-out for using customer prompts/responses for model improvement or training. That opt-out can be scoped to an account or to specific tenants. If you require a strict prohibition on using your prompts/responses to improve models, we will:
  - Add a training-exclusion clause to the DPA (we will provide suggested wording), and
  - Flag your account at the ingestion layer to exclude content from any model improvement pipelines.

3) Residency and transfers: for APAC deployments we support Provisioned Dedicated Tenants in SG (or private deployments) so data stays inside the requested region. If you need hosted but restricted transfers, we use standard transfer mechanisms (SCCs or equivalent), and can additionally offer customer-managed KMS to minimize exposure.

Attachments: Im attaching a short DPA snippet that illustrates the training-exclusion language and a simple dataflow diagram showing where logs, keys, and model telemetry touch the stack.

Next steps I propose:
- Rishi (ccd) to propose target DPA language.
- Lauren to scope a Dedicated Tenant in SG + timeline and cost.
- Quick sync (30 min) with your product/procurement next week so we can confirm wording and implementation details.

Would Tue or Wed morning your time work?

Best,
Priyom Das
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: redwood_dpa_training_clause_snippet.pdf (pdf), sg-dataflow-diagram.png (image)

Hi Sara / Priyom / Lauren,

Following up with proposed contractual language and implementation notes. High-level: yes, we can contractually prohibit use of BrightAssist prompts/responses for model training or model improvement unless BrightAssist gives written consent. Below is an extract wed suggest for the DPA / Schedule A: 

--- DPA extract (proposed) ---
"Customer Content" means prompts, system messages, and all Assistant Responses provided to or generated by the Service on behalf of Customer.
"Model Use Restriction": Redwood Inference shall not use Customer Content for model training, model fine-tuning, or for inclusion in any model improvement datasets, nor shall Redwood permit any of its subprocessors to use such Customer Content for those purposes, except where Customer gives prior written consent.
--- end extract ---

Operational notes: 
- Subprocessors: we will provide a current subprocessor list and notify you of any changes 30 days in advance; for APAC-dedicated deployments we limit the subprocessor set to those with regional presence and with contractual commitments aligned to the Model Use Restriction.
- Telemetry & logs: we can disable customer-level telemetry that contains prompt fragments; platform metrics (latency, error rates, token counts) will still be collected for SLA/ops but can be stored within SG tenant boundaries.
- Transfer mechanics: when transfers are required, we will rely on SCCs or a legally equivalent mechanism; for customers that need additional assurance, we can enable customer-managed encryption keys (CMK) so Redwood cannot decrypt exported material without your authorization.

Ive attached the DPA snippet and the SG dataflow diagram showing the tenant boundary and telemetry knobs. If BrightAssist needs tighter constraints (e.g., explicit subprocessor forbiddance), please flag that and well route to execs for approval.

I will push a redline to the DPA draft by EOD today so procurement has something to kick off review.

Rgds,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Legal, Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: redwood_dpa_training_clause_snippet.pdf (proposed text), sg-dataflow-diagram.png
